submissions.title: Voters back data center limits in 40 of 41 ballot measures across 10 states
submissions.excerpt: Voters back data center limits in 40 of 41 ballot measures across 10 states
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: In the Nov 3, 2026 general election, voters approved local data-center restrictions or outright bans in 40 of 41 local ballot measures across 10 states, per Ballotpedia's Nov 4 tally (Venable's Nov 4 legal alert reaches a similar conclusion; other trackers using different cutoff times/methodologies report 38-44). Ohio accounted for roughly half the measures (~21). Only one community (in North Dakota) passed a pro-data-center measure. Not tied to a single tracked project — flagging as a general, nationwide siting-climate signal that may be worth its own restriction-type record rather than a per-project one. Counts were still being finalized in the days after the election; verify against Ballotpedia's final certified tally before recording a hard number.

submissions.title: Arkansas lands $6B data center deal
submissions.suggestedProjectName: AVAIO Digital "Leo" Campus (Wrightsville, Pulaski County, Arkansas)
submissions.note: New project not currently tracked: AVAIO Digital's ~760-acre AI data center campus ('Project Leo') near Wrightsville, Pulaski County, AR, ~10 miles south of Little Rock. Phase 1 capex reported at $6B; full buildout reported up to $21B (Arkansas Business) — treat the $21B figure as press-report derived, not company-confirmed. Initial Entergy Arkansas interconnection contract reported at 150 MW, with AVAIO saying demand could grow toward 1 GW at full buildout (site power / utility-contracted basis, not IT load; AVAIO has not disclosed an IT-load figure). AVAIO also reportedly plans >500 MW of behind-the-meter gas generation plus a 75 MW solar array on site. Surfacing now because the project is the subject of active Nov 2026 litigation over county zoning — see the companion SITING RESTRICTION submission below for the same project.

submissions.title: AVAIO asks judge to halt Pulaski County data center ordinance enforcement amid lawsuit
submissions.excerpt: AVAIO asks judge to halt Pulaski County data center ordinance enforcement amid lawsuit
submissions.suggestedProjectName: AVAIO Digital "Leo" Campus (Wrightsville, Pulaski County, Arkansas)
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: AVAIO Data Partners filed a motion for a preliminary injunction on Thursday, Nov. 4, 2026, in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Arkansas, seeking to block Pulaski County from enforcing its new data-center ordinance against AVAIO's Wrightsville-area campus while AVAIO's underlying federal suit proceeds. The suit argues the county's regulations are preempted by federal authority over interstate electric transmission and commerce, and separately alleges Arkansas FOIA violations (withheld public records). The county's own 1-year data-center moratorium — which had exempted AVAIO's project — failed to take effect after the county clerk discovered a vote-counting error (miscount) in the quorum court tally; it is unclear whether the quorum court can revote on the original (non-exempting) ordinance. The county's defense rests partly on a 2023 Arkansas law barring local governments from banning data-center permits. No ruling on the injunction had been reported as of this research run — worth a follow-up check for the court's decision.

submissions.title: Fort Worth advances proposed data center moratorium following late-night public hearing
submissions.excerpt: Fort Worth advances proposed data center moratorium following late-night public hearing
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: Fort Worth, TX held the first of two legally required public hearings on a proposed 90-day data-center construction moratorium on Nov. 10, 2026; reporting indicates every speaker at the hearing favored the moratorium. Under the process the council began in August, a second vote is required roughly 28 days after the first, and final passage needs a three-fourths council supermajority (not a simple majority) — the moratorium is not yet in effect. Context: Fort Worth separately approved a revised site plan for Black Mountain's reported ~$10B, 187-acre data-center campus (Lon Stephenson Rd/Forest Hill Dr) amid this same debate; that project is not currently in the tracker and may warrant a separate new-project proposal if a megawatt figure can be confirmed (none found in this research pass — only dollar/acreage figures). Publication date for this article is approximate (day after the Nov. 10 hearing) — please confirm the exact date before promoting.
